_comment: agy-bridge config. Tasks resolve a CAPABILITY -> ordered candidate models (or an explicit chain override). The bridge tries each; first success wins; if all fail it exits 3 with a claude_fallback sentinel. Every model has a per-Mtok price (model_prices) so cost/savings are computed honestly for ALL backends, including subscription ones (NOT $0).
_agy_note: agy ids = EXACT `agy models` display strings; agy SILENTLY routes an unknown id to a default, so run.py refuses any id not in known_agy_models. agy token usage is NOT exposed by the CLI -> agy token counts are ESTIMATED (chars/4, flagged). agy auth is flaky per-call (auth-blip -> run.py retries once).
_zai_note: zai = z.ai GLM Coding Plan (subscription, Anthropic-compatible). Token in ZAI_API_TOKEN or token.env. Real server -> exact usage in response, and it ERRORS on a bad model id (no silent fallback).
_agy_models_seen: 2026-09-16 (refreshed from `agy models`): Gemini 3.8 / 3.7 / 3.6 Flash (High/Medium/Low), Gemini 3.1 Pro (Low/High), GPT-OSS 120B (Medium), Claude Sonnet 4.6 (Thinking), Claude Opus 4.6 (Thinking). Gemini 3.5 Flash is GONE from agy as of this refresh; its model_prices entries are kept so historical log rows still price correctly on replay.
_time_routing_note: off by default: time routing may only be turned on once peak_wib is filled from measured data (`--analyze`). 'advisory' logs the reorder it would do without applying it.

agy._flat_rate_note: Antigravity subscription is flat monthly (see subscriptions.antigravity_agy); marginal cost per call is $0. run.py records actual_usd=0 for agy and keeps the per-Mtok figure in metered_equiv_usd so the data isn't lost. zai/kimi stay metered here: both have a real per-token quota (zai_quota_mult, promo_until) that can run out, so their per-call cost still reflects quota consumption, not $0.

kimi.credential_hint: Kimi Code Console (kimi.com/code/console) -> create API Key; set KIMI_CODE_TOKEN or token.env
kimi._note: Kimi Code SUBSCRIPTION endpoint (flat monthly via Kimi membership), Anthropic-compatible, plain API-key auth (not OAuth). Metered alternative would be api.moonshot.ai/anthropic + platform.moonshot.ai key. Confirm the model id in the console (e.g. kimi-latest); wired into cross-lineage for a distinct lineage vs GLM/Gemini/GPT-OSS. Price below is a per-Mtok SEED for the cost counterfactual only (real billing is the flat subscription, see subscriptions.kimi_code).

quota._source: z.ai dashboard 2026-06-24: GLM-5.2/GLM-5-Turbo share one usage quota; peak 14:00-18:00 UTC+8 = 13:00-17:00 WIB.
quota._promo_note: Off-peak charged 1x (not 2x) through end of Sep 2026; after that set offpeak to 2x. Peak is always 3x.

zai._retired_note: Subscription ended; retired from all chains 2026-07-27. Kept for cost-history replay and easy restore.

9router.credential_hint: 9router runs on 127.0.0.1:20128 and holds the upstream subscription itself; no token is set here.
9router._note: Local LLM router proxying the SAME Antigravity subscription the `agy` CLI uses, plus providers agy cannot reach (bpm/*). Wired in as a FALLBACK after the agy entries, never ahead of them: it adds a daemon to the critical path, and if it is not running every call through it fails. What it buys is no subprocess per call and exact token counts, where the CLI path estimates them. TEXT ONLY -- 9router accepts audio, discards it, and returns invented text (verified across 7 models on 2026-08-21), so audio must never be routed here.

gemini.credential_hint: Free tier: create a key at https://aistudio.google.com/apikey, then `echo 'GEMINI_API_KEY=...' >> .env` in the workspace root
gemini._note: Google's own OpenAI-compatible endpoint, reached with a plain API key instead of the Antigravity CLI's OAuth. This is the backend a brand-new user can actually turn on: same free key that makes meeting transcription work, no subscription, no CLI. Kept behind the agy entries so an existing Antigravity install is unaffected.

groq.credential_hint: Free tier: create a key at https://console.groq.com/keys, then `echo 'GROQ_API_KEY=...' >> .env` in the workspace root
groq._note: Free tier, very fast. Model ids move faster here than at other vendors, so confirm with `run.py --setup`, which lists what the key can actually see rather than trusting the id below.

ollama.credential_hint: Local Ollama, no token. Start it with `ollama serve` and pull the model with `ollama pull gpt-oss:120b`. Running in WSL or on another box: set OLLAMA_BASE_URL=http://<host>:11434/v1
ollama._note: Ollama's OpenAI-compatible endpoint (/v1), NOT /api/generate. /v1 is what returns parsed content and a tool_calls array; the native path leaves the model's raw harmony JSON in the body, which is how tool calls end up printed as text instead of executed. Local weights, so marginal cost is 0: flat_rate records actual_usd=0 and keeps the published gpt-oss rate in metered_equiv_usd for the counterfactual. LAST in every chain on purpose. A local 120B is the fallback for when nothing else is reachable, not the lead.

model_prices._unit: USD per 1,000,000 tokens, [input, output]. List/published rates as of 2026-06-24. Subscription backends are NOT free; this is their per-Mtok equivalent.
model_prices._sources: Claude: metacto/tldl 2026. Gemini: ai.google.dev/pricing. GPT-OSS: pricepertoken. GLM: estimated ~2.6x cheaper than Gemini Pro (confirm at z.ai pricing).
model_prices._gemini_38_price_note: gemini-3.8-flash at the INTRODUCTORY rate $0.75/$3.75 per Mtok, published, valid through 2026-12-31. Standard $1.50/$7.50 takes effect 2027-01-01: bump it then, or every saving figure against Claude reads 2x too good. Source: ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing

subscriptions._note: Flat monthly outlay in USD for each subscription backend, shown on the dashboard as context and NEVER folded into per-call cost. Zeros here mean 'not subscribed'. Put your real figures in models.local.json, which is gitignored.

peak_wib._note: Quota demote windows per backend, [startHour, endHour) in local time, 24h. EMPTY by default and deliberately so: a demote window copied from someone else's vendor dashboard reorders your chains for a quota you do not have. Fill this in models.local.json only after `--analyze` shows measured peaks in YOUR telemetry.

capabilities._note: capability -> ordered backend+model candidates, grounded in model strengths/context. Tasks reference one of these. Cost is NOT the only axis here (context window + lineage matter); the cost dashboard reveals where a choice does/doesn't save vs its claude_fallback so chains can be retuned from data.
capabilities._bulk_cheap_note: OWNER DECISION 2026-07-04: Gemini Flash stays lead for harvest even though the cost log shows GLM is cheaper per-call. Reason: the Gemini (agy) subscription is rarely used otherwise, so subscription utilization outweighs the per-call savings. Do NOT 'optimize' this back to GLM-first based on agy_usage_log alone.
capabilities._draft_flash_note: OWNER DECISION 2026-07-22: Gemini 3.5 Flash promoted to HEAD of the draft chain (was glm-5.2-first), same rationale as bulk-cheap -> utilize the idle Gemini/agy subscription. glm-5.2 stays fallback #2. reasoning/critic intentionally NOT changed: GLM keeps the lead there for reasoning depth + cross-lineage diversity.
capabilities.image: NOT handled by the bridge -> use the gemini-image skill. Default image model is gemini-3-pro-image ('Nano Banana', pro 3.1 tier; set 2026-07-22); imagen-4.0 only when true aspect-ratio control is needed.
capabilities._zai_retired_note: z.ai / glm-5.2 REMOVED from every chain 2026-07-27: the GLM Coding Plan subscription is no longer active and live probes return an error, so leaving it in a chain only bought a guaranteed failed attempt before the Gemini fallback answered. Gemini via agy now heads every capability. The zai backend definition is kept under backends.zai so re-subscribing is a one-line restore, but do NOT re-add it to a chain without a passing --doctor probe first.

harvest.intent: Bulk read transcripts/MOM/Slack/Dashboard -> raw facts, no synthesis. Cheap + fast + big context.

critic.intent: Adversarial / cross-model second opinion. Three distinct lineages (GLM/GPT-OSS/Gemini) for genuine diversity.

research.intent: Deep-research fan-out / non-Claude reasoning for diversity. Strongest reasoning first.

draft.intent: Generate content drafts (social posts, SEO fixes, copy) on the cheap strong writer GLM 5.2; specialist agents call this for generation. Falls back to Claude sonnet for voice/quality.

_known_agy_models_note: Populated from `agy models` by `run.py --setup --write`, per account. run.py refuses any id not in this list because agy silently routes an unknown id to a default; an empty list here means 'ask the CLI', not 'allow anything'.
